title: Fold Arrangement
content: ### Objective Fold Seam Allowances, collars and cuffs before activating the Simulation for better stability. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Fold Arrangement 3D Toolbar ▶ Fold Arrangement ### Operation 1. After arranging Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Fold Arrangement 3D Toolbar ▶ Fold Arrangement → The entire Internal Line/Shape of a 3D Garment appears. 2. Click on an Internal Line/Shape to fold. → The folding Gizmo appears. 3. Rotate the red or green axis along the blue circle as desired. → The selected area's Pattern is now being folded accordingly. → If the pattern is symmetrical, it is folded symmetrically. (ver 11) ※ Note: Folding Internal Line/Shape is also available after simulating/draping the Garment.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for folding seam allowances, collars, and cuffs in a 3D garment simulation to enhance stability.

title: Delete Pin
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary pins. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins → The selected pin is now being deleted. ※ Note: Selecting a created pin while holding W key on keyboard also deletes the pin.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to delete unnecessary pins from 3D garments using various methods in the editing menu.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Open/Save Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Save a created tape measure in .mea file format. Open a saved tape measure to reuse it. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Open /Save ### Operation #### Open Measurement 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Open → Open File window appears. 2. Select a desired file and click Open. #### Save Measurement 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Save → Save File window appears. 2. Select a desired location to store. 3. Enter a desired file name and click Save. → .mea file is now being created.
content_description: This web page enables users to easily save and open tape measures in .mea file format for convenient reuse.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Delete Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Delete tape measures that are no longer in need. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Delete ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Delete 2. Select a tape measure to delete. 3. Click on the Delete icon. → The selected tape measure is now being deleted.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a straightforward method to delete unnecessary tape measures from their avatar editor.

title: FILE: Export Joint Keyframe Animation with FBX
content: ### Objective Allows users to export both the garment and avatar together, without losing joint animation. The joint animation is currently exported with keys at every frame for the duration of the motion. ### Location File ▶ Export ▶ FBX ▶ Option ▶ Joint Animation ### Operation 1. Import an FBX containing a rigged character with joint animation as an Avatar, with the box next to 'Joint Animation' checked (found under the "Object" section). 2. Create a garment for the character, or add a garment option from the Library, at a desired pose from the Avatar's animation. → Simulate in the 3D Window to drape the garment onto the Avatar. 3. Once complete, navigate to the File menu location, select 'Export', then select 'FBX'. 4. Choose 'Export All' in the Export FBX pop-up window. 5. Click on 'OK'. 6. Open the resulting FBX file in another 3D software package. → Observe that the Avatar's joint animation has been exported (keyed at every frame).
content_description: This page provides a step-by-step guide for exporting garments and avatars together with preserved joint animations in FBX format.

title: Move/Rotate Pattern with Gizmo
content: ### Objective Move or rotate Patterns, objects, Avatar Joints and etc. with the Gizmo. ### Location #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard ※ Note: Preferences for the Divided Gizmo can be accessed via: Main Menu ▶ User Setting ▶ 3D ▶ Gizmo ▶ Divided Gizmo ### Operation #### Move 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard → The Gizmo appears. 2. Move by dragging in a desired direction. ※ Note: #### Move Y Axis Click > Drag the green arrow (pointing up) up and down to move the Pattern vertically. #### Move X Axis Click > Drag the red arrow (pointing right) left and right to move the Pattern horizontally. #### Move Z Axis Click > Drag the blue arrow (pointing forward) forward (upwards on the screen) or backwards (downwards on the screen) to pull or push the Pattern to the front and back. #### Yellow Square Box Free drifting to horizontal/vertical directions. ![Gizmo](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438002535449) #### Rotate 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard → The Gizmo appears. 2. Mouse over the Gizmo's rotation axis. → The mouse cursor shape is now being replaced to (Rotate). 3. Click ▶ Drag in the desired direction to rotate the corresponding object. ※ Note: #### Rotate Y Axis Click > Drag the green radius left and right to rotate the Pattern centered on the vertical line. #### Rotate X Axis Click > Drag the red radius up and down to rotate the Pattern centered on the horizontal line. #### Rotate Z Axis Click > Drag the blue radius the Pattern with the central point as the axis. ![Gizmo](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438002843929)
content_description: Learn how to effectively move and rotate patterns, objects, and avatar joints using the Gizmo in your 3D design environment.

title: Distribute
content: ### Objective Distribute Patterns or/and Internal Shapes/Lines by designated intervals (ver2.5.0). ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶ Horizontally/Vertically ### Operation 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Lines/Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶ Horizontally/Vertically →The Distribute Window appears. 4. Enter the desired Spacing value and select OK. →The selected Patterns and/or Internal Lines/Shapes are distributed horizontally or vertically by the designated intervals.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for distributing patterns or internal shapes and lines at specified intervals using the right-click pop-up menu in a 2D design toolbar.

title: Unified Gizmo
content: ### Objective Use an unified Gizmo to select, rotate and move elements. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click Pattern ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click Pattern → Once a pattern is selected (clicked), the Unified Gizmo appears. ※ Note: Unified Gizmo can be set up at Preference. Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 3D ▶ Gizmo ▶ Unified Gizmo ※ Note: Gizmos for Avatars appear when X-ray Joint Points (Shift+X) is on or in OBJ format file.
content_description: This web page provides a guide on using the Unified Gizmo for selecting, rotating, and moving elements within the 3D Toolbar.

title: Open/ Save Topstitch Style
content: ### Objective Open or save preset or custom Topstitch to easily use it in other Project or Garment files. ### Location #### Open Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Open #### Save Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Save ### Operation #### Open 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Open → The File Browser window appears. 2. Select the desired Topstitch file and click Open. → The selected Topstitch file opens and all properties are reflected in the Property Editor. #### Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Save → The File Save window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and assign Topstitch name. Then, select Save. → The Topstitch is saved as a *.sst file and all properties are saved.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a concise guide for users to easily open and save preset or custom Topstitch styles for use in various project or garment files.

title: Fasten/Unfasten Button
content: ### Objective Fasten or unfasten buttons to style the Garment as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Fasten Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Fasten Button ### Operation #### Fasten Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Fasten Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Fasten Button 2. Click on a button, then click on its corresponding buttonhole in either the 2D or 3D environment, then continue on to the remaining buttons and buttonholes. → The buttons move above the buttonholes. → Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes appear (ver2.5.0). #### Unfasten Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Fasten Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Fasten Button 2. Click on fastened buttons and buttonholes in either the 2D or 3D environment. → Buttons are now unfastened and return to their previous location. → Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes disappear (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: * To fasten multiple buttons and buttonholes at once, click and drag in the 2D window to select all buttons to be fastened, then click the first buttonhole to be paired with the buttons (ver4.0.0). * To unlock multiple buttons and buttonholes, click and drag on all fastened buttons and buttonholes. * Fastened buttons and buttonholes can now be moved (ver4.0.0).
content_description: This web page provides instructions for fastening and unfastening buttons to customize your garment's style in a 2D or 3D environment.

title: Reset 2D Arrangement
content: ### Objective Spread and arrange the entire or the selected patterns in the 3D window identical to 2D window state. ### Location #### Selected Pattern 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ right-click menu on a 3D pattern ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) #### All Pattern Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) ### Operation #### Selected Pattern 1. Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement identical to 2D window state. ※ Note: Press Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ right-click menu on a 3D pattern ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) → The selected Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state. #### All Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) → The entire Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for resetting the arrangement of 3D patterns to match their corresponding 2D states, either individually or collectively.

title: Show Statistics (ver. 12.1)
content: ## Feature Overview You can check various information related to the garment through the 'Show Statistics' ## Steps Follow the indicated guideline below to open 'Show Statistics'. Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show Statistics View Options icon (3D Window) ▶ Environment Display ▶ Show Statistics ## End Result Information related to the garment will be displayed at the left bottom corner of the 3D Window. ![hud_statistics.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438419772057) Please refer to the table below for the information items. Vertices | The number of the vertices ---|--- Edges | The number of the edges Triangles | The number of the triangular meshes Faces | The number of the entire faces Patterns | The number of the pattern pieces Trims | The number of the trims Sewings | The number of the Seam Line Pair Group CPUs | The number of the activated CPU Fps | Frames per Second, Simulation speed. F | Garment, gravity time I | Linear system time P | Garment-garment proximity time S | Garment-garment collision time O | Avatar skinning time SK | Avatar skinning + Joint animation time E | Time excluding clothing simulation and avatar skinning in the overall simulation. R | Rendering time. UI | UI update time. T | Simulation + Rendering + UI update time.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to access and interpret garment-related statistics within the 3D window of the software.

title: Reset Button Style Property
content: ### Objective Reset button item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset → The button item properties are now being reset back to default value.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to resetting button item properties to their default values in version 2.5.0.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide All Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Show or hide all of the tape measures in the window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Avatar Measurements ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Avatar Measurements → All Avatar tape measures are now being displayed or hidden.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to easily show or hide all tape measures for their avatar within the 3D display window.

title: Convert to Curve Point (AI Bezier Curve)
content: ### Objective Convert AI Bezier Curve's Segment Points to Free Curve Points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point ### Operation #### AI Bezier Curve 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2. Right click on the AI Bezier Curve or the Segment point on the curve. → The right click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Convert to Curve Point. → The selected AI Bezier curve is converted to a Free Curve as its AI Bezier curve handles disappear and necessary Free Curve Points are added to maintain its original curvature. #### AI Bezier Curve Handles 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Curve Point 2. Click on the AI Bezier curve to be converted. → Its AI Bezier curve handles appear. 3. Right click on the end point of the handle and select Convert to Curve Point on the pop-up menu. → Its original curvature is maintained as Free Curve Points are added.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for converting AI Bezier Curve segment points to Free Curve points while preserving the original curvature.

title: Apply Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Apply buttonhole styles or fabric material (.zfab) onto buttonholes as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ### Operation #### Apply Buttonhole Style In Property Editor 1. Click on a buttonhole and select a buttonhole style in the Property Editor. → The selected buttonhole style is now being applied to the buttonhole. #### Select A Buttonhole And Apply Buttonhole Style 1. Select a buttonhole. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Assigned to Selected Patterns → The buttonhole style is now being applied to the selected buttonhole. #### Select A Buttonhole And Apply A New Buttonhole Style 1. Select a buttonhole. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Assigned to New Fabric → A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for applying various buttonhole styles and fabric materials to buttonholes using the Object Browser and Property Editor.

title: Create 2D Button Measurement
content: ### Objective View button position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. Select a button with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center 3. Select the desired 2D measurement options of the left/right/up/down. → The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for viewing and adjusting the 2D measurements of a button's position within the Pattern outline using the Button Property Editor.

title: Button List Window
content: When creating a button, The Default Button is applied as default setting and displayed in the button list window. Once the Default Button style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.
content_description: This web page explains the functionality of the Default Button in our application, detailing how it is set, modified, and its persistence across sessions.

title: Express Air Pressure
content: ### Objective Use the Pressure value to create an effect of air or padded materials such as padded jumpers, pillows, cushions, balloons, etc. ### Location Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Pressure ### Operation 1. Select a Pattern to express pressure with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Pressure 3. Adjust the value as desired.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using pressure values to simulate the effects of air-filled or padded materials in design applications.

title: Line Tack on Avatar
content: ### Objective Create lines on Garment and avatar and tack to each other by lines. (Ver. MD7) ### Location 3D window tool bar Line tack on Avatar tool ### Operation 1. Select the tool according to the Location above. 2. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. 3. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. Once a line is created on the garment, 3D garment will be transparent, can create line on the avatar directly. 4. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. 5. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. * During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. * Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. * When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and connecting lines on garments and avatars using the 3D window tool, enabling users to design intricate shapes with ease.

title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Tape Measurement
content: ### Objective Take avatar's measurements such as arm length, back length from projected points. Basic Tape Measurement measures following by its surface curves. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement 2. Click on a point to begin the length measurement. → Temporary line appears in purple. 3. Click on any points that need to be included in the process, and double click to end the measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for accurately measuring an avatar's dimensions using Basic and Surface Tape Measurement tools within a 3D environment.

title: Show/Hide Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Show or hide all buttons and buttonholes. ### Location 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Button ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Button → All buttons and buttonholes are now being hidden. 2. Follow the indicated guideline once again. → All hidden buttons and buttonholes are now being displayed.
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to provide users with the ability to easily toggle the visibility of all buttons and buttonholes in a 3D garment display.

title: OBJ TRIM: Glue OBJ Trim
content: ### Objective Glue 3D Trims onto Garments and simulate together (ver3.0.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ ### Operation #### Glue OBJ Trim 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Select desired OBJ file and click OK to load. 3. In the pop-up menu, select Load as Trim for the Object Type, and click OK. 4. Click the loaded OBJ with the Select/Move tool. → Gizmo for the selected OBJ appears. 5. Click on the Glue icon next to the OBJ Gizmo, then mouse over the desired location. → OBJ preview tags along the mouse. 6. Click on the desired location. → Selected OBJ automatically attaches to the place. 7. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and angle. ※ Note: To cancel the arrangement, press Esc on the keyboard. 8. Activate Simulation. → OBJ is now being simulated along with the rest of the Garments. ※Note: You can select multiple OBJ trims and move or rotate those by using Gizmo. (ver. 11 ) Delete OBJ Trim 1. Right click on the OBJ trim. → OBJ is now being selected and a pop-up menu appears. ※ Note: Relevant menu above does not appear for OBJ trims that are not glued to the Garments. 2. Click on Delete to remove it. → Selected OBJ is now being removed from the Garments.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for importing and gluing 3D OBJ trims onto garments in version 3.0.0 of the simulation software.

title: Align
content: ### Objective Align Patterns and Internal Shapes based on various standards (ver2.5.0). ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/ Internal Shape) ▶ Align ▶ Left/ Center/ Right/ Top/ Middle/ Bottom ### Operation 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/ Internal Shape) ▶ Align ▶ Left/ Center/ Right/ Top/ Middle/ Bottom →The Patterns or/and Internal Shapes align to the Pattern or Internal Shape that is right clicked on. ※Note: You can also align Pattern outlines or Internal Lines using the 2.png Edit Pattern tool. However, be mindful that the aligning segments may transform their Patterns or Internal Shapes.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for aligning patterns and internal shapes using the right-click pop-up menu in version 2.5.0, ensuring precise arrangement according to various standards.

title: Edit Sewing Line Length
content: ### Objective Adjust Sewing Line length. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing 2. Click and drag either end point of the Sewing Line to adjust its length. ※ Note: While clicking and dragging the end of the Sewing Line in the 2D Window, right-click and type in the Distance Moved or Total Length in the Moving Distance window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting the length of the Sewing Line in the sewing design interface.

title: Mirror Paste Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Copy and mirror paste buttonholes (ver2.5.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 2. Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. 3. Right click on the copied buttonhole then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. → Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click on a desired location to paste the buttonholes. ※ Note: * Before pasting buttonholes in place, right click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttonholes can be manually input for multiple copy-and-paste. * When buttonholes are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to efficiently copy and mirror paste buttonholes in the design software.

title: Add Arrangement Point
content: ### Objective Add new Arrangement Point on the Bound Volume as needed. ※ Note: Without corresponding Bounding Volume, the Arrangement Point is invisible. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Arrangement Point ▶ Add Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Arrangement Point ▶ Add → A new arrangement point called "Arrangement Point" is now being created at the bottom of the A-Point list in the Arrangement tab, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2\. Set details for Arrangement Point. Name | Changes the name of the Arrangement Point. ---|--- Arrangement | Arrangement BV | Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point to be placed. X | Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y | Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset | Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction | The direction in which the Pattern wrapped around the Avatar. ※ Note: #### Symmetric Arrangement Point Setting Name the Arrangement Point with an underscore and location (R for right and L for left) at the end of the name to set Symmetric Arrangement Point. The name must be the same as the name before the underscore and the alphabet. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default (ver3.0). _R _L Follow the indicated steps below to save the Avatar and Arrangement Points, and reload to apply the setting. Light-blue outer line appears around the Symmetric Arrangement Point. #### Save Avatar: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶ Avatar #### Save Arrangement Point: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Arrangement Point ▶ Save
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding and configuring Arrangement Points within the Avatar Editor, ensuring they are properly linked to Bounding Volumes for visibility.

title: Convert: Curve Points & Segment Points
content: ### ### Objective Convert multiple Segment Points on single or multiple Patterns to Curve Points. Convert multiple Curve Points on a single or multiple Patterns to Segment Points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select all Segment Points / Curve Points to be converted to the other point type. 3. Right click to access the pop-up menu. Then select Convert to Curve Point / Convert to Segment Point. Select the option Maintain Curve or Convert Only. (ver. 2024.2) → All selected Point type - Segment points / Curve Points are converted to the other type. ### Convert Options (ver. 2024.2) Maintain Curve | Adds curve points automatically to the line to maintain the line curvature / straight line result. ---|--- Convert Only | Convert without adding curve points on the line. The curved line / straight line result will be affected slightly.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for converting Segment Points to Curve Points and vice versa within 2D patterns, allowing users to optimize their design workflow.

title: Cut/ Cut & Sew
content: ### Objective Cut a single 2D Pattern into two or more pieces using Internal Lines (ver2.3.0). ### Location #### Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern #### Trace Tool (ver2.4.0) Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace ### Operation #### Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut & Sew. → The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut & Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. #### Trace Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut & Sew. → The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut & Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. ※ Note: With the Trace tool, you can Cut or Cut & Sew Patterns using the Baselines as well.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for cutting and transforming 2D patterns into multiple pieces using internal lines and trace tools within the editing software.
